hazards.feel-for-leak: You reached out to feel for the leak with your hand. Hydrogen burns nearly invisible and a high-pressure leak can cut skin — only the detector looks for leaks.
hazards.force-damaged-nozzle: You pushed the nozzle with the scuffed seal onto the receptacle. A damaged seal leaks at the connection under fill pressure; use the spare and report it.
hazards.fuel-with-cell-running: You started to connect the nozzle with the fuel cell system still running. Shut down first so the system is not drawing from the tank while it fills.
hazards.phone-on-island: You carried your phone onto the fuelling island. Phones and other electronics are kept outside the line because a spark is all a hydrogen release needs.

interrupts.alert: An older diesel service truck has pulled up beside the fuelling island and its driver is climbing out with a lit cigarette.
interrupts.cue: Stop the driver at the line and send them outside the island — the fill display waits for no one else.
interrupts.kind: A diesel truck pulls up beside the island
interrupts.missNote: You stayed on the display while the driver walked toward the island smoking; they were at the dispenser before anyone told them to stop.
interrupts.why: A lit cigarette at the edge of a hydrogen island during a fill is the exact ignition source the painted line is meant to keep away, and stopping it at the line comes before anything else.
interrupts.wrongNote: Stop the driver first — an open flame approaching the island is answered at once.

interrupts.alert: The portable hydrogen detector is beeping a low-battery warning as you start tracing the hiss near the tank rack.
interrupts.cue: Swap to the charged spare detector from the station cabinet — the trace waits.
interrupts.kind: The portable detector warns of a low battery
interrupts.missNote: You kept tracing with the failing detector; it went quiet before it reached the tank valve and the leak read as clean.
interrupts.why: A detector running out of battery can stop reading without anyone noticing, and a silent detector over a leak looks exactly like a clean fitting; the spare is kept charged for this moment.
interrupts.wrongNote: The spare detector first — a failing instrument is swapped before its reading is trusted.

name: Hydrogen Fuel Cell Equipment and Fuelling

passRule.note: stars >= 2 and no unsafe action (WebXR/shared/records.js passed())

steps.cue: Read the posted steps: shut down, ground, connect, fill, disconnect — and where the dispenser's emergency stop is.
steps.prompt: Read the posted steps: shut down, ground, connect, fill, disconnect — and where the dispenser's emergency stop is.
steps.title: Read the island's posted fuelling instructions
steps.why: Hydrogen dispensers differ in how their nozzles lock and how the fill is started, and the posted instructions are the station's own sequence for this dispenser; reading them each time is what keeps a habit from another island from becoming a nozzle pulled under pressure.

steps.cue: Phone into the locker and anything that can spark or flame into the bin before crossing the island's painted line.

itemNames.lighter-bin: lighter into the bin outside the line

steps.prompt: Phone into the locker and anything that can spark or flame into the bin before crossing the island's painted line.
steps.title: Leave ignition sources outside the island
steps.why: Hydrogen ignites with very little energy across a wide range of mixtures with air, so the fuelling island is kept free of sparks and flames by rule rather than judgement; the painted line is where that rule starts, and it applies to everyone crossing it.

steps.cue: Spreader down, parking brake on, fuel cell system shut down from the key before any hose is touched.
steps.prompt: Spreader down, parking brake on, fuel cell system shut down from the key before any hose is touched.
steps.title: Park, lower the spreader, shut the machine down
steps.why: A top pick with its spreader raised or its fuel cell still running is a machine with stored energy and a live hydrogen supply, and the fill is done with both brought to rest; shutting down first also stops the system drawing from the tank while it is being filled.

steps.cue: Carry the dispenser's ground clamp to the machine's bonding point and clip it on.

drag.missNote: Not clipped — carry the clamp all the way to the machine's marked bonding point and close it on the bare metal tab.

steps.prompt: Carry the dispenser's ground clamp to the machine's bonding point and clip it on.
steps.title: Clip the static ground before the nozzle
steps.why: Gas flowing through a hose can build a static charge, and a spark at the nozzle is the ignition the whole island is designed to avoid; the ground goes on first and comes off last so the machine and dispenser stay at the same potential throughout.

steps.cue: Check the nozzle's seal ring and the machine's receptacle for damage, dirt or ice before connecting.

itemNotes.scuffed-nozzle-seal: The nozzle's seal ring is scuffed and flattened on one side — it may not seal against the receptacle, and a poor seal leaks at the connection under fill pressure.

steps.prompt: Check the nozzle's seal ring and the machine's receptacle for damage, dirt or ice before connecting.
steps.title: Look into the nozzle and receptacle
steps.why: The connection between nozzle and receptacle holds the full fill pressure, and a damaged seal or grit on the receptacle is the most common place for a leak to start; the dispenser's spare nozzle or a call to the station tech is the answer, not a harder push.

steps.cue: Carry the spare nozzle to the receptacle and lock it until the latch shows engaged.

drag.missNote: Not locked — push the nozzle squarely onto the receptacle and turn the lever until the latch shows engaged.

steps.prompt: Carry the spare nozzle to the receptacle and lock it until the latch shows engaged.
steps.title: Seat the good nozzle on the receptacle
steps.why: A hydrogen nozzle locks onto the receptacle mechanically before the dispenser will start, and a nozzle that is not fully locked is one the dispenser should refuse; seating it square and checking the latch indicator is how you know the dispenser's check is not the only one.

steps.cue: Stay at the dispenser and keep the fill pressure inside its band until the dispenser stops the fill.
steps.holdBreakNote: The fill left its band before the dispenser stopped — stay at the display for the whole fill; that is where the emergency stop is.
steps.prompt: Stay at the dispenser and keep the fill pressure inside its band until the dispenser stops the fill.
steps.title: Watch the fill pressure climb to the stop
steps.why: The dispenser controls the fill rate to keep the tank inside its temperature and pressure limits, and a person standing at the display can stop it at once if the reading does something the fill should not; walking away during a fill leaves nobody at the emergency stop.

steps.cue: Pass the portable detector over the receptacle and tank fittings and commit once the reading settles clean.

gauge.label: H2 ppm
gauge.missNote: The detector had not settled — hold it still at the fitting until the reading steadies before you commit.

steps.prompt: Pass the portable detector over the receptacle and tank fittings and commit once the reading settles clean.
steps.title: Check each fitting with the portable detector
steps.why: Hydrogen is colourless and odourless, so a leak cannot be seen or smelt, and a small one can go unnoticed until it finds an ignition source; a portable detector passed slowly over each fitting after the fill is how the tank's connections are checked.

steps.cue: A faint hiss near the tank rack — trace it with the detector, never with a hand or a rag.

itemNames.tank-valve-leak: detector alarm at the tank valve

itemNotes.tank-valve-leak: The detector chirps at the tank's shut-off valve — a small leak at its packing, found by the instrument, and a reason to stop, isolate and report.

steps.prompt: A faint hiss near the tank rack — trace it with the detector, never with a hand or a rag.
steps.title: Trace the faint hiss with the detector
steps.why: A hydrogen flame burns nearly invisible in daylight and a high-pressure leak can cut skin, so a hand feeling for a leak is the one test that must never be used; the detector finds it from a safe distance and tells you which fitting to isolate.

steps.cue: Press the island's emergency stop to shut the dispenser's supply, and call the leak in.
steps.prompt: Press the island's emergency stop to shut the dispenser's supply, and call the leak in.
steps.title: Press the dispenser's emergency stop
steps.why: The island's emergency stop closes the dispenser's supply valves and stops the fill system, and pressing it on a confirmed leak is what keeps more gas from feeding the release while the machine is made safe; it is placed where you can reach it without crossing the leak.

steps.cue: Close the tank shut-off, key out, lock and tag the machine before the mechanic removes the compartment cover.
steps.prompt: Close the tank shut-off, key out, lock and tag the machine before the mechanic removes the compartment cover.
steps.title: Lock out before the fuel cell compartment opens
steps.why: The fuel cell stack and its high-voltage output stay hazardous with the machine keyed off, and 29 CFR 1910.147 controls both the gas and the electrical energy before a cover comes off; the tank shut-off is part of the isolation, not an extra.

steps.cue: Keep the island clear behind the painted line until the station tech confirms the release has dispersed.
steps.holdBreakNote: People drifted back across the line before the tech gave the all clear — hold them until the release has dispersed.
steps.prompt: Keep the island clear behind the painted line until the station tech confirms the release has dispersed.
steps.title: Hold everyone behind the island line while it vents
steps.why: Hydrogen is much lighter than air and disperses upward quickly in the open, which is why fuelling islands are outdoors and uncovered; holding people back for the short time it takes is what keeps anyone from walking into the release before it has gone.

steps.cue: Record the machine, the fill, the swapped nozzle seal and the tank valve leak, with the time you pressed the emergency stop.
steps.prompt: Record the machine, the fill, the swapped nozzle seal and the tank valve leak, with the time you pressed the emergency stop.
steps.title: Log the fuelling and the leak
steps.why: The fuelling log is how the station tech knows the nozzle seal needs replacing and how the maintenance shop knows why this top pick is tagged; a leak that is only told in passing is a leak the next shift finds again.

tagline: A hydrogen fuel cell top pick at the terminal's fuelling island: the posted instructions read, ignition sources left outside the island, the machine parked and shut down, the static ground clipped, a frosted and scuffed nozzle seal found and swapped for the spare, the nozzle seated, the fill pressure watched to the stop, the portable detector reading clean at every fitting, a hiss at the tank valve found with the detector rather than a hand, the dispenser's emergency stop pressed, the compartment locked out before the cover comes off, and the fuelling logged
